title: Sinfonia concertante in E-flat major for violin and viola
hook: A conversation between two soloists, violin and viola, written in Salzburg after a journey that went wrong.

painting.title: The Mozart Family
painting.pairingNote: Painted in Salzburg in 1780–81, the year after the Sinfonia concertante; Leopold holds his violin, and on the wall hangs the portrait of Mozart’s mother, who had died in Paris during that journey.

facts: Mozart wrote it in Salzburg in 1779. He had just come home from a fruitless journey in search of a better post (1777–79), which took him to Mannheim and Paris. His mother, who travelled with him, died in Paris in July 1778.

In Paris the [[sinfonia-concertante|sinfonia concertante]], a piece for several soloists and orchestra, was then highly fashionable. Mozart had tried something similar before, in a Concertone for two violins (1774), and he started another, for violin, viola and cello, that he left unfinished.

The viola part is written in D major, a semitone lower than everyone else, and the instrument is tuned a semitone higher: a [[scordatura|scordatura]]. The tighter strings make the viola brighter and help it carry over the orchestra. On modern instruments the retuning is less common.
Mozart wrote out the cadenzas himself, so the soloists play his music there too; his autograph of the slow movement’s cadenza is in the collection of the Veste Coburg.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a grand opening from which the two soloists emerge together (I), a lament in C minor sung by both in turn (II), a quick, high-spirited chase (III).

movements.heading: Allegro maestoso
movements.summary: A long, stately opening for the orchestra, with a slow build-up from soft to very loud. Then the violin and the viola appear together, almost unnoticed, on one high held note. From that moment the movement is a dialogue: one instrument says something, the other answers, a little lower or in a new key. It is laid out like a concerto movement, in [[sonata-form|sonata form]].

mainIdeas.name: The opening
mainIdeas.description: firm, ceremonial chords for the whole orchestra, in a dotted rhythm.

mainIdeas.name: The build-up
mainIdeas.description: a short figure repeated higher and higher over a held bass, growing louder.

mainIdeas.name: The dialogue
mainIdeas.description: a melody played by the violin and answered straight away by the viola, or the other way round.

stops.hear: The whole orchestra, loud and grand: firm chords in a dotted rhythm
A long build-up: a short figure repeated higher and higher over a held bass, from very soft to very loud
stops.happening: A [[crescendo|crescendo]] in the style of the Mannheim orchestra, which Mozart had just heard

stops.hear: Out of the orchestra, the violin and viola appear together on one high held note
The violin plays a melody; the viola repeats it a moment later, in its darker voice
A new key and a new tune, still shared between the two
stops.happening: The second theme, in B-flat major

stops.hear: Darker keys; the soloists pass short phrases back and forth over a restless orchestra
The orchestra’s opening music returns in the home key, and the soloists take up their first melody again
The orchestra stops on a held chord; violin and viola play alone, imitating and answering each other
stops.happening: The [[cadenza|cadenza]], Mozart’s own, written for both soloists

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: The orchestra alone, firm and festive

notice: Listen to the soloists’ entry. They do not start a new tune: a single high note seems to grow out of the orchestra.
Follow one phrase through the dialogue. When the viola takes it over, the same notes sound warmer and darker.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Father and son: Igor Oistrakh plays the violin, and his father David, best known as a violinist, plays the viola and also conducts. On the Spotify album the Sinfonia concertante is tracks 7–9, after the Violin Concertos Nos. 2 and 4 and before the Concertone.

movements.heading: Andante
movements.summary: A slow lament in C minor, one of Mozart’s saddest movements. The orchestra sets out the sighing melody, then the violin sings it, and the viola answers in its lower, darker register. The two soloists keep taking turns and then begin to overlap, until they share a long cadenza of their own.

mainIdeas.name: The lament
mainIdeas.description: a slow, falling melody in C minor, first in the orchestra.

mainIdeas.name: The answer
mainIdeas.description: the same melody passed from violin to viola, lower and darker.

mainIdeas.name: The consolation
mainIdeas.description: a gentler passage in E-flat major.

stops.hear: The orchestra alone plays a slow, sighing melody, quietly
The violin enters alone with the melody, high and sorrowful
The viola takes up the same melody, lower and darker
The mood softens: the soloists share a gentler, more hopeful phrase
The sighing opening returns, and the soloists take it up again
The orchestra stops; violin and viola play alone, one imitating the other

stops.label: Last 50 seconds
stops.hear: A quiet close for the orchestra, still in C minor

notice: Listen to the moment when the viola first answers the violin. It is the same melody, but the lower instrument makes it sound older and sadder.

movements.heading: Presto
movements.summary: After the lament, a fast, bright finale. A bouncing tune comes round again and again, and between its returns the soloists race through quick passages, throwing short phrases to each other faster and faster.

mainIdeas.name: The main tune
mainIdeas.description: quick and bouncing, first in the orchestra.

mainIdeas.name: The soloists’ race
mainIdeas.description: fast runs and leaps, passed from one instrument to the other.

stops.hear: The orchestra alone: a quick, bouncing tune
The violin plays the tune; the viola repeats it
Fast runs, tossed between violin and viola
The bouncing tune returns in the orchestra
The exchanges get shorter and quicker: a bar for one, a bar for the other
stops.happening: The soloists’ race at its fastest

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: Both soloists and the orchestra together, ending with loud chords

notice: Count how quickly the soloists answer each other near the end. The conversation that was slow and grave in the Andante is now almost breathless.

threads.title: Two equal voices
threads.body: Neither instrument is the star. Each idea is offered by one and taken up by the other, often in turn, often a little lower.

threads.title: The viola’s bright tuning
threads.body: Mozart asked for the viola to be tuned up a semitone, to make its voice stronger next to the violin.

threads.title: Echoes of the journey
threads.body: The sinfonia concertante was a Parisian fashion, and the long orchestral build-up of the first movement recalls the famous orchestra of Mannheim, both cities of Mozart’s recent tour.
